dispositions.notes: Direct citation, [L2], used at steps 1.1 and 5.1. Read from disk. Its application already supplies everything the bound form now demands: the host graph is the original G of its own Statement, the W_i are parts of the equitable gamma-regular partition of V(G) obtained at step 1.1, so W_i is a subset of V(G); the pairs are gamma-regular of density at least eta IN G (step 2.1 deletes the irregular and low-density pairs from G, and step 4.1's copy of H sits in G'); W_i != W_j on every edge of H because step 2.1 deleted the within-part edges, so the endpoints of an edge of H lie in distinct parts; and |W_i| >= n/(2M) >= N once n_0 is large. Binding G narrows nothing it uses and removes the ambiguity about which graph its 'injective copies' were counted in. Its contract quote of the cited Statement was re-pointed at the repaired text; no item edit.

Direct citation, [L1], used at steps 3.1 and 4.1. Read from disk. It does not invoke the counting lemma as a black box: step 3.1 borrows the greedy argument's retained-fraction constant and step 4.1 re-runs that argument with a per-pair required relation. Its own host sets W_1..W_h are the vertex sets of one ambient graph in which its densities d(W_i,W_j) are measured, which is exactly the configuration the bound form describes, so nothing it cites was narrowed away. Its contract quote of the cited Statement was re-pointed at the repaired text; no item edit.

Transitive consumer only: its Facts cite thm-self-regular-representative-subsets, thm-induced-counting-lemma-for-regular-pairs, def-graph-edit-distance-and-epsilon-far and def-induced-copy-number, and never the counting lemma directly. Its representative sets W_i are subsets of the partition parts V_i of V(G) for the G fixed in its own Statement, so the ambient graph its chain rests on was already bound. Unaffected.

Transitive consumer through thm-induced-counting-lemma-for-regular-pairs ([L1]); it never cites the counting lemma. Its three host sets are pure cross-pairs of a single graph, complete pairs of density 1 and an anticomplete pair of density 0, and it exhibits them as the zero-error, 0-regular model of that lemma. A single ambient graph is already explicit in the construction, so binding G upstream changes nothing it relies on.

Transitive consumer through thm-induced-graph-removal-lemma ([L1]); it never cites the counting lemma. It is a concrete construction in one named graph — K_n with the three internal edges of a triple S deleted — and it uses the induced removal lemma only for the fact that induced removal permits additions as well as deletions. No regularity hypothesis and no counting bound is invoked, so the repair cannot reach it.
